principles: Preserve CLI user surface byte-for-byte where behavior matters.
Move cohesive helper groups out of cli-engine.ts without turning this story into lifecycle dispatch refactor.
Keep compatibility exports so existing task imports continue compiling.
Use executable smoke coverage for parser/help/alias/dry-run behavior, not prose-only confidence.
drivers: cli-engine.ts still centralizes parser/help/alias surface logic after B-74a0 and B-6e69.
This work touches command invocation ergonomics, so regressions are user-visible immediately.
B-57b5 owns lifecycle dispatch and INIT_CHECK metadata handling and must not be preempted here.

options.name: A: Extract three focused CLI surface modules with compatibility exports
pros: Keeps parser/help/alias responsibilities separated and easy to review.
Matches B-74a0 and B-6e69 extraction pattern.
Allows targeted smoke tests for each CLI surface.
cons: Requires careful import wiring around ToolDef, CommandPolicy, owner lease help, and version branding.
Leaves runCli special dispatch still large until B-57b5.

options.name: B: Extract only parseFlags now and defer help/aliases
pros: Less chance of touching help text.
cons: Leaves most of B-a776 scope in cli-engine.ts and does not materially reduce the god-file surface.
Forces another story to re-open the same help/alias/dry-run area.

options.name: C: Rewrite parser/help/alias handling into a new command router
pros: Could produce a cleaner long-term command layer.
Might reduce future lifecycle dispatch work.
cons: Too much behavior risk for this split round.
Would overlap B-57b5 lifecycle dispatch ownership and make review harder.

chosen: A: Extract three focused CLI surface modules with compatibility exports
rationale: A gives a meaningful cli-engine.ts reduction while preserving exact command behavior and avoiding the lifecycle dispatch area reserved for B-57b5.

preMortem.scenario: Flag parsing silently changes repeated arrays or JSON body behavior.
preMortem.trigger: parseFlags extraction loses normalizeFlagKey or Zod array handling details.
preMortem.consequence: Existing commands reject valid CLI invocations or parse them differently.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep parser implementation mechanically equivalent and run cli-argument ergonomics plus new CLI surface smoke.

preMortem.scenario: Nested aliases stop resolving, especially lattice host/status/config forms.
preMortem.trigger: Alias map extraction changes aliasStart or consumed argument count behavior.
preMortem.consequence: Documented multi-word commands fail or dispatch to unknown command.
preMortem.mitigation: Add smoke coverage for flat commands and lattice-prefixed multi-word aliases.

preMortem.scenario: Help/dry-run text regresses and users lose safety guidance.
preMortem.trigger: Help renderer extraction forgets dryRunHelpLine or owner lease help block ordering.
preMortem.consequence: Dangerous/preview commands become less discoverable and REVIEW catches late.
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke story_advance, story_reconcile, test_auto, host_install help output including dry-run and owner lease text.

preMortem.scenario: Story accidentally drifts into lifecycle dispatch extraction.
preMortem.trigger: Worker moves story_advance/init/recover special cases while touching nearby runCli code.
preMortem.consequence: Scope overlap with B-57b5 and possible INIT_CHECK metadata regressions.
preMortem.mitigation: Scope contract explicitly protects lifecycle dispatch behavior and smoke asserts no lifecycle special dispatch files/blocks moved beyond imports.
